newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kohl sees NATO deal this year after Yeltsin talks.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees NATO deal this year after Yeltsin talks.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Saturday after talks near Moscow with President Boris Yeltsin that there were still differences of opinion with Russia over NATO expansion but that he expected to settle those this year.

"I think that this year we will find a rational solution which will make NATO enlargement (into eastern Europe) possible and will at the same time respect the security interests of all partners concerned," Kohl told a news conference.
"There are still some differences of opinion," he said, referring to Russia's objections to plans to grant membership of the Western defence alliance to former communist states in eastern Europe.
"But we evaluated a couple of ideas which I will discuss with my NATO colleagues over the next couple of days on the telephone," he added, mentioning U.S. President Bill Clinton.

Earlier, Yeltsin was quoted as saying that he and Kohl had agreed to continue discussions on NATO expansion. It was the Russian president's first meeting with a Western leader since his heart bypass operation on November 5.

Western leaders see Yeltsin's return to the Kremlin after a long absence caused by his illness and July's presidential election campaign as a chance to end to apparently shifting policy in Moscow on NATO enlargement.
